item.title: Re: The Mushroom Men
item.content:encoded:
While there are a number of great ideas here, there's nothing really solid. Some of the ideas you have in the Elevator Pitch should be moved into the Central Narrative, and then you need to build up the Mushroom Men in terms of what they are, what kind of society they have, and why they are fighting SCP 610.

While we get an idea of what you are trying to do, the problem is that there is nothing really about the Mushroom Men themselves here, and with nothing here they're just a generic race for the sake of having a new race. Nail down some of the specifics, and then go for it. We don't need a thesis on them, just something to make them breathe (so to speak) a little.

item.title: Re: SCP Idea: Aggressive Earworm (Seeking Greenlight)
item.content:encoded:
1) You may want to do a search on this; there are a number of similar concepts on the site.

2) You need to show some of the stages and effects. Specifics tend to sell better than general details.

3) "Hook" shouldn't be a summarization of the SCP; it needs to be a reason why it's interesting. That is, why is the SCP worthy of attention from a narrative perspective. Is the earworm causing a major problem, and if so how? Or is the earworm showing how pop culture is a bad idea? Or even how pop music is just all that dangerous?

There has to be something from a narrative perspective that makes it interesting, and this is the section to show why it's worth looking at.

The picture of the underground lake is stunning and I was pretty interested to learn about cooking for vampires, but I didn't enjoy the characterization.

+ show block
– hide block

I kept being pulled out my enjoyment at the beginning by the inconsistent tone of the in-universe author. Sometimes they sound like an ancient vampire:

I have stayed in many hotels in my long unlife, many which have catered exclusively to hemovores like myself.

The venue wants to feed us, and we want to eat! But how to make food that we are actually capable of consuming?

and other times they sound like a cooking YouTube channel.

Every part of the place is specifically designed to be a great experience for all hemovores to relax.

The solution Chaz came up with: just use a lot of blood in the cooking process. If the food is bloody enough, then we'll be able to eat it and keep it down.

I recommend leaning more into the old vampire speech because you mostly stick to that in the latter sections and it works.

Meanwhile hunt section isn't that exciting. It's slow, but because we're seeing it from the vampire's point of view, there's no tension to be heightened by the slower pace. You could introduce some by giving the human a chance to defend themselves, but I think you'd be better off just making the human sacrifice a willing employee of Ambrose's; then you can at least get interesting dialogue about what working under him is like.

The Chaz interview doesn't do anything to flesh out the idea of 'Chaz is a horrible sophisticated monster' more than the rest of the article or even the new Chaz articles do.

We've grown stale as a brand.

I decided I wanted to start pushing the envelope, breaking new ground.

There was plenty of room to expand, innovate and start trying new material. I could finally break free of my shell and start doing what I really wanted to do.

Lots of long hours in the kitchen. Got fairly messy at times.

These are all character traits we learned in Do You Like Huey Lewis and the News. We even already learned that he cooks with blood in that tale! I'd be much more interested to know why Chaz chose to become a vampire, that lifestyle requires dedication and I want to know how he juggles it with being a chef! Him knowing all that would also give the reveal that he's a regular dude way more punch. Right now, the paragraphs about Chaz walking into the light unscathed don't enhance and honestly just slow the reveal down. He doesn't feel enigmatic — he still feels like celebrity chef Hannibal Lecter.

item.title: Re: Lengthy SCP Idea
item.content:encoded:
Ok I am limited by 400 words and it's kinda hard to get everything across, but I mean that it isn't a single item that changes depending on what people think it is, and is whatever that is closest to it. It's an exact copy of what one person thinks it is, and can be more than one thing. Using the explosion example, someone can think it is just a folding chair, they can sit in that chair, and appears sitting on nothing, and someone who doesn't think it's a chair won't feel the chair/can't sit on it, but imagine that person thinks it's an explosive. Now they can move that explosive, and the chair the other person see doesn't move, the SCP is now 2 objects, while stilling being one SCP, and not SCP-1/A/whatever, both are just the "standard" SCP. OK so now that explosive is set off, and explodes, because the explosion would have the same effects as a normal one, the chair isn't moved, but there is still damage to the room and the other person, who thinks it's a chair. The reason for redactions is for people to think it's something harmless so it can't do something, and if someone thinks it's something that lives and just naturally destroys things, like a Keter that can easily escape it's room that can also cause massive damage. Only qualification is that someone has to think something that is it's name (SCP number) to be physical to only that person.

tl;dr - It takes only one person to change the scp, creating another thing which only is physical to that person, and scp can harm things and affect inanimate objects, and other people indirectly.

Just tell me if you think anything seems wrong, again I don't think I can get the exact thought in my head across.

item.content:encoded:
So, to start with, you aren't supposed to link sandbox drafts just yet if I recall. If you haven't been published on the wiki before you publish drafts you have to come here and get the greenlight here. That doesn't mean you get around the restriction by dumping your draft into this forum. There's a form you need to fill out in less than 400 words. If I have to fill it out, then so do you. Its not fair to everyone else who followed the rules and read the instructions for you to try and jump the que.

And I'm going to put a huge damper on your idea. Because any cyborg or android can do what's described in this article if they have a usb port and a wireless connection.

+ show block
– hide block

A long time ago I had a multiverse fanfic universe, and my main character had a steadily evolving cybernetic arm. One of her bad habits was to use it to play music while she was fighting, and when told she'd give her position to an enemy away she simply had it play in her head in the middle of battle so that she was the only one hearing it.

Then there's the ghost in the shell anime/manga universe, where this cyborg's behavior would be seen as a computer virus, and thus he'd be seen as the victim of a terrible crime. Because his free will would have been overridden by a hacker. This is a universe that dwarfs what your guy can do, because your average person can surf the internet inside their head, backup their memories, replace any part of their body with one that's almost a perfect realistic replica, you get the picture. They've even got more than enough augments to make a cyborg into a superhero, and they don't even go into the more gory ways this technology could be used to save lives.

The SCP Universe even has hyper realistic androids and cyborgs of varying degrees. There's Anderson robotics, and the Asimov's Lawbringers MTF that fights them. There's MTF Tau-5 Samsara as well, which played a prominent role in the story of Site 13.

In general, I suggest you do more research into futurism concepts. In fact I recommend this youtube creator, as he has an entire 28 video long playlist on the ins and outs of integrating technology into the human mind and body as well as what androids and cyborgs would realistically look like and what machine intelligence tropes will probably never exist due to their impracticality. He also explains the limitations of this technology, important to keep in mind, and examines examples from actual science fiction including the grandfather of robot centric sci fi, Isaac Asimov. Just don't forget to grab a drink and a snack. ;) https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCZFipeZtQM5CKUjx6grh54g/playlists

I strongly recommend this channel to anyone looking to write a realistic science fiction story, (or SCP) because of the sheer level of detail he goes into. And as a retired military engineer, he knows a lot more about the subjects he covers than I do.

Please collapse long posts as a courtesy to our mobile users. —RockTeethMothEyes

item.title: The Mushroom Men
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre (Optional):

Page Layout (Optional):

Elevator Pitch: A tribe of sentient fungus people clawing out a living on the edge of the Lake Bikal Secure Containment Zone…

  • See the funerary cave they maintain and a peculiar stone age corpse within, deformed from a long, losing battle against SCP 610.
  • Hear of their mycelial network, like a brain unto itself in complexity, capable of healing, administering medications and poisons, and communicating directly with the land itself.
  • Imperiled by climate change, can the Foundation keep them from starting tribal warfare with SCP 610 for control of the shores of Lake Bikal?

Central Narrative: A more ecologically based view of the OG Sarkic Anomaly, the amazing environmental flexibility of fungi and their age old conflict with bacteria, musings of what a sentient mushroom might look like, and whether there really is a separation between flesh, nature, and machine.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: Loosely inspired by a cave painting and the work of Professor Paul Stamets. I tried to capture the uses and habits of fungi and their importance to the environment in an SCP, from the best known to the theoretical. They also pose a different kind of breach risk to the Foundation, one I attempted to base on real life concerns over the human consequences of climate change.

Additional Notes: OMG I did it! A proposal that expresses everything I wanted to in less than 400 words!!!!!

item.title: Re: Lengthy SCP Idea
item.content:encoded:
Hey there An_Person, I'll be critting your idea today!
Note that I am not an official reviewer, so take what I say with a grain of salt. With that being said, let's begin the crit!

+ Open Section-by-Section +
Woooooooosh

Elevator Pitch

So I have two problems with the concept you're putting forward. One logistical, the other originality:
Firstly, if people who don't know the entity exists can't interact or perceive it in any way, how did the anomaly become known to the Foundation in the first place? What happened?
Secondly, this concept is very similar to that chair (no, not that chair, the other one). They are both anomalies whose properties are completely dependent on the majority perception of them. As your concept stands, it seems like an almost exact clone of SCP-2950, just less interesting.

Central Narrative

Your narrative is extremely vague. All you've told the people reading is that there is a heavily modified document with some interviews and discussions in it, without any actual story arc. I'd give you more feedback on this, but there really isn't much there.

Hook/Attention Grabber

From what I'm seeing, this just seems needlessly complex. It's an entity that changes based on what people think it is, there doesn't need to be a whole bunch of redactions and blackboxes. Having those would in fact make people more curious about what it could be (i.e due to those redactions it might make people think it could be something very dangerous) and completely defeat the purpose of the document.

+ Open General Thoughts +
I'm very doubtful about this

The narrative is boring, and the hook wasn't interesting, but the main problem with your idea is, well, that it's basically a copy of SCP-2950. Everything that you're presenting has, unfortunately, already been done by that SCP and executed better. Personally, I'd recommend either heavily reworking this idea or scrapping it due to the immense difficulty in pulling it off successfully.
I'd also recommend checking out the Guide Hub for some great essays on ideation and story-ing, it's a great resource for aspiring writers on this Site such as yourself!

And finally, to sum up your idea in one sentence1:
An entity that changes based on what people think it is.

Anyway, that's it for my crit today. Thanks for reading, and I hope this helps!

Footnotes
1. This is to give you an idea of the bare bones of what a critter sees when they read your summary. You may find something you don't like here, or find that we're getting the wrong impression.

item.title: Re: Super Mario Syndicate
item.content:encoded:
I was asked here via PM.

So the biggest issue I'm seeing here is that this doesn't actually have anything to say. The premise seems like it's going to explore capitalism, police brutality, etc, but then it just sort of devolves into grindhouse style spectacle.

To that end I think that this needs, like… purpose? Something deeper than strange aesthetics. A reflection of society, an engaging story, an intriguing mystery, something. The video game industry has significantly changed since the release of Super Mario 3. Devs are coming up against contract work, crunch time, publishers that find microtransactional garbage far preferable to interesting games. There's a lot that can be said about this, and I think the best version of this does say something about it.

item.title: SCP Idea: Aggressive Earworm (Seeking Greenlight)
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlight: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Genre: Comedy, Drama

Page Layout: Standard article with a set of media players, multiple updates/addenda.

Elevator Pitch:
Generic copyright free music is anart created to infect and replace all other forms of music. This SCP is an 'album' of several similar songs originally created as a protest of music censorship, following the "if I can't have it, nobody can" trope. This music can take many forms depending on the context, but is always recognized by the presence of Ukulele, Glockenspiel, Whistling, and Rhythmic Clapping. The music has a memetic effect where listeners can't get the song out of their head, and start to hear it in place of other forms of music. This effect is felt most strongly by other artists and creators. The music also imparts a feeling of constant happiness on them, and listeners are compelled to share the music through their own work.

Central Narrative:
The music spreads primarily through online transmission, with anartists uploading the music to various music sharing/streaming sites. The Foundation is notified to its existence when news of 'undeletable songs' start appearing in online music forums. By the time they're able to track down the sources and start to counteract the infectious music, the original artist disappears/escapes, though the music is continually posted in new locations. The spread is contained through intensive screening of streaming sites, and SCP agents are able to delete the anomalous frequency patterns from the data to discretely disable the effects in places where it cannot be otherwise removed outright. However, those already affected by the song have steadily worsening effects, eventually all sound they hear is in the form of the music. Perhaps a log to show someone deafening themselves or needing to communicate through writing in a sound isolation chamber to try and mitigate the effects. The effects are only curable through intensive Amnestic treatment, and careful avoidance of even the non-anomalous versions of the music.

Hook/Attention-Grabber:
Due to the widespread use of such music in the real world, the reader will likely be familiar with the form of music described, showing how far it has 'already' spread. The initial comedy of cheesy generic music being an SCP will also contrast well with the more serious implications and lasting effects shown later in the article.

Description:

SCP-5134 is a global effect where social media posts having exactly 13 Likes for some periods of time increases the statistical tendency of horrible events relating to the posts occurring in the real world. Some Foundation theorists consider it a manifestation of a new trend of digitally-defined anomalies, others consider it a Strange Attractor baked into statistics, and also a third school, consider it a projection of the collective power of superstitions, social media outrage and self-fulfilling prophecies.

Feedback is as follows:

+ JuiceNotJava
– JuiceNotJava

I have written my first comment prior to this one, but the article had since then been revised so yeah.

Deleted an article by Duganist at -12 with three staff votes, standard deletion process.

Description:

SCP-5923 is the catalyzation effect of hastening the arrival of The Big Rip by viewing a time series of measurements of distant quasar redshift, making projections from them, and tracking a progressive increase in the negative pressure ratio of the dark energy in the universe. By tracking these measurements consciously, the investigating scientist creates an observer effect that intensifies the dark energy in the universe and expedites the t-0 moment where our universe ends.

Feedback is as follows:

+ ManyMeats
– ManyMeats

I like the underlying concept. At first I was going to take you to task for just memeing up a novel scientific concept and trying to pass it as an SCP but there is something more here. In total, however, this article suffers from too much speculation and a long trip to arrive at a somewhat subtle pay-day.

I could definitely see this working with a few more refinements. For example, the conprocs are very long and the bit about the meticulous cover-up with amnestics in chocolate and their water is…way off tone for the rest of the piece.

+ Riemann
– Riemann

There's a lot of things that can be said here, but I think it may suffice to point out first and foremost that a Big Rip scenario is not anomalous. It's a natural consequence of the dark energy equation-of-state parameter being more negative that -1, something that comes out fairly naturally from FLRW equations.

Current best data from the Pantheon sample strongly indicates that w = -1.026, which is within error (not shown here) of w = -1. So while it's unlikely that the big rip will occur, there's nothing in our current understanding of cosmology that precludes this.

There seems to be some reference to "the more people think that the big rip will happen the more negative w becomes", but it's buried in a confusing mess of other thoughts and random diatribes about unrelated things. The fact of the matter is that the cat's sort of out of the bag here, and largely has been since Riess and Perlmutter's discovery of the accelerating expansion of the universe in 1998. It's many people's jobs to discuss the value of w - there's been a Nobel prize assigned for that, and it's fairly critical to an ongoing field of physics.

70% of this is describing non-anomalous science. The other 30% is a tangle of self referential procedures and comments designed to scaffold the fundamentally non-anomalous nature of this article.

-1

The wobble in w comes from quasars which have huge variance in range, which I understand to be the source of the ?? moment. Big Rip definitely came off as freaky in 2005 when first suggested. w at -1.026 I think implies a rip some e's prior to the projected decay of protons, which is e42-44 years, we're talking a rip sometime deep inside the Degenerate Era. Whereas, you set this thing to -10, we're getting kind of spooky.

Yeah, the issue here is that quasar's aren't fantastic at constraining w right now. Back in 98 we barely had anything more than the Philip's Relationship - MLCS was clunky as heck - for Type Ia cosmology. Riess just barely pulled above the threshold for proving acceleration, he definitely was nowhere near getting w = -1. And that's kind of where quasar cosmology is today. Modern Type II cosmology is also fairly wack, largely because we don't have any sort of SALT or MLCS2K model of standardising brightness.

Point being, I guess, if you want to continue with this, maybe focus more on the "the more people realise w is negative the more negative it gets", rather than focusing on the non-anomalous outcome of that. And yeah, the containment procedures as-is are fairly implausible.

But most readers won't take you to task over cosmological errors, just me

item.title: Re: Threadmother (Seeking Greenlight)
item.content:encoded:
I think you should drop the AI aspect. This isn't an artificial intelligence but the embodiment of man's first attempts to communicate with the unknown. Think of a Kami investing the animus of a place, that's what this did. And it served as the middleman between humanity and those beyond, gods/demons whatever. Such that all information passed along was abstracted through two layers (however the entity communicates with other things, and then the way the entity communicates with human beings) two levels of interpretation that could lead to misunderstandings.

+ show block
– hide block

Moreover, I think the connection of ancient Sumer is tenuous, how would they have known about it? Did they also worship it? Has there been people constantly caretaking it through the centuries?

Additionally, I think you should expand the narrative, what is the arc of the story (you've given us alot of backstory about the researcher and the thread mother, but not so much what the arc of the article is about?)

Finally, I don't think Threadmother is such a great title. a) there are not threads, b) the whole "mother" connotation for ancient primordial entities is sorta well trod territory. Would suggest something a little different, something that speaks of originality and its role in guiding humanity as messenger (if you take my above suggestion to heart)

item.title: Re: Cockroach Party
item.content:encoded:
Howdy hey, didn’t expect to be critting roaches today but here are my notes anyway. (Hey that rhymes)

+ Overall
- Overall

You did well with the humor. I like all the random rituals that the cockroaches are doing. I’s funny how arbitrary the lists of items are. The rest of the pacing is good too. The addendums are sudden but I like it.

My main question is about the test logs, namely why is the Foundation giving valuable resources to roaches? I understand most of the supplies, the Foundation can easily afford to give away hydrochloride acid or carrots or whatnot. I’m mainly concerned about the amnestics and the telekill alloy. Both of those are things the Foundation can’t just buy, and think of the paperwork required for a researcher to use any amount of telekill. I don’t think they’d consider this test worth it

I don’t think there’s a name for anomaly detectors, I’ve never heard of that concept before. It’s not necessarily a bad idea but you might want to think twice about if you want to do it. Sometimes it can feel a little uncreative if you just make something up to contain your anomaly. Especially because this could be contained without that by just using security cameras.

For refining the logs, you might want to decide whether these are parties or rituals. You seem to be leaning towards rituals in the logs but the impression I’m getting from you is that they are supposed to be parties. If they’re parties then you might want to add more party-like events. If they seem like traditional parties it’ll add a new level of humor. If “parties” is just what the cockroaches call their rituals however then you have the right style. You might want to make the earlier tests seem more like practice rituals and less like parties though.

+ Line-by-line
- Line-by-line

The home at 314 Crowley St. is to be hermetically sealed with plastic no thinner than 50 millimeters

I have a couple notes on this part. First, use house, not home. Home implies that it’s welcoming, it’s not really the word that the Foundation would use. Second, there’s no real reason to give an address. You can just say, “the house containing SCP-XXXX” the people reading this don’t really need to know where it is. Third, you realize hermetically means airtight right? You gave no impression that the roaches can survive without air.

Recent estimates have placed the population of the colony at upwards of 10,000 individuals

That’s around the amount they had to when they performed the ritual that made -2. Wouldn’t “manageable levels” be below that?

SCP-XXXX has displayed multiple behaviors and properties not present in non-anomalous cockroaches…

This whole paragraph feels a bit choppy. I wish I could explain more how to revise it but I’m not really sure. It might not even be a problem and I’m just looking at it too hard.

chalk was ground into dust and multiple instances were coated

You might want to clarify SCP-XXXX, because when I first read this I thought they were coating the paper.

unspecified amount, 3 kg supplied

Why three kilograms? That’s kind of an arbitrary number, and a decently large amount at that. I’d understand one kilogram but three just seems random.

When held, permanently affords subject the ability…

So is it permanent or when held? I’d suggest “If held…”

SCP-XXXX engaged in a ritual lasting approx. 45 minutes

No reason to abbreviate approximately.

MTF Lambda-6 were subsequently called in to contain SCP-XXXX-2.

Why aren’t there security guards at the location? Usually locations have security personnel to, if nothing else, ensure nosy kids don’t go inside. You should put that in your containment procedures as well.
